prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip places the work surface, dishes, and the camera wearer’s lower foreground within roughly 0.3–0.8 m, with the standing person across the table about 1–1.8 m away and the rear kitchen surfaces about 2–4 m away. Across frames 1–4, that person remains in front of the wearer, shifting from near the centre to the right while turning partly side-on; in frame 5 the person is closer, roughly 0.7–1.2 m away, on the right and partly cut off by the frame edge. Foreground objects occlude the lower body, while the person occludes portions of the counter and cabinets; the map makes these near-to-far layers clearer than RGB alone. Metric distances are only rough because the map is monocular, and bright foreground regions merge together, erase object boundaries, and occasionally assign inconsistent depth to the person’s head and torso.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates a person, dining table, bowls or cups, a bottle, chairs, and—in the last frame—a microwave, clarifying which overlapping RGB regions belong to distinct objects. In frames 1–4, one person stands across the table about 1–1.8 m in front of the wearer, with tableware within roughly 0.3–0.8 m of the wearer and also within the person’s arm’s reach; the person shifts from centre-left toward the right and becomes more side-facing. In frame 5, a person occupies the right foreground about 0.7–1.2 m away, facing mostly left and downward rather than directly toward the wearer, while the microwave is behind and above them; another partial person-labelled region near the centre-right appears inconsistent with the RGB. The masks reveal occlusion boundaries and partly out-of-view objects better than RGB, but they are fragmented, omit much of the cabinetry and small clutter, confuse some bowls and cups, and provide no direct metric depth or reliable gaze direction.
descriptions.pose: The pose map locates the person’s upper body and both hands across frames 1–4: the torso is in front of the wearer, the hands are below the shoulders over the nearby table, and the hands remain close together and within the person’s reach. The skeleton changes from a roughly frontal orientation in frame 1 to increasingly rotated or side-on configurations by frame 3, then returns to a more upright, near-frontal configuration in frame 4; face keypoints suggest the head is generally angled downward toward the work surface rather than clearly looking at the wearer. Relative to the camera wearer, the person is roughly 1–1.8 m away in these frames, while the hands and tabletop are somewhat nearer, but pose alone cannot establish accurate metres, scene layout, object distances, or what is behind the body. It makes limb placement and body rotation easier to read than RGB despite torso and hand occlusions, but several joints are geometrically distorted in frames 2–3, and frame 5 contains no detected pose even though a nearby person is visible in RGB.
